messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty ALERT — CRITICAL: prod-us-west-1 gpu-nodepool exhausted. queue growth > 3000. autoscaler unable to add nodes. paging oncall.
pd-bot: Trigger: gpu-queue-surge-prod, escalation -> linh, latency > 1.2s token tail, error rate up 4x.
linh (oncall): I'm here, joining bridge. starting quick triage — checking autoscaler logs and nodegroups.
anya (sre): tagging in — I see recent spike at 03:12 UTC, backlog started spiking after a deploy. likely autoscaler failed to create instances.
micah (runtime): holding on, traffic spike looks like a batch job replaying; we can fallback some jobs to cpu-models to reduce gpu demand if needed.
jordan (infra): looking at ASG and LT in us-west-1-gpu-nodes. describe shows LaunchTemplate version v4, cluster-autoscaler expected v3. also iam:PassRoleDenied in instance profile logs.
linh (oncall): copy. can you paste the autoscaler error?
jordan (infra): ```Cluster Autoscaler: Failed to create instance in nodegroup us-west-1-gpu-ng-1: LaunchTemplate version mismatch (expected 3, got 4) -> Attempting fallback failed: UnauthorizedOperation: iam:PassRoleDenied for arn:aws:iam::123456:role/RedwoodNodeProfile```
anya (sre): that's our smoking gun — autoscaler tries to spin up nodes with launch template referencing a new instance profile that hasn't been given PassRole to the autoscaling service role. policy drift from the deploy.
linh (oncall): what's immediate customer impact? micah?
micah (runtime): inference queues for heavy-llm customers are throttling. Host-level rps down ~65% for affected models. Some clients getting 429s; internal fallback to smaller models triggered where available. We'll need ~20 GPUs to get stable.
sam (eng): I can stand up a temporary nodegroup with an older LT that has correct instance profile. should be fast via terraform apply?
jordan (infra): terraform apply will require plan/approve and might be slow. I can manually create a temporary ASG with correct LT v3 via console, set desired=20. manual approach will speed it.
linh (oncall): do it. while you do that, can runtime divert new requests to cpu variants? micah please coordinate.
micah (runtime): initiating route change: shifting low-priority routes to cpu-model pool and enabling shorter timeouts for long requests. patching routing rule now.
anya (sre): oncall checklist: 1) create temp nodegroup -> jordan 2) attach correct instance profile -> jordan 3) scale desired -> jordan 4) remove taint from temp nodes or add toleration -> micah 5) check autoscaler config and restore passrole permission -> infra follow-up.
jordan (infra): console-created ASG up, instances launching. instance ids: i-0a1b2c3d... give me 60s.
linh (oncall): monitoring pod pending count, queue length.
anya (sre): autoscaler logs now show new attempts succeeding against temp LT.
jordan (infra): instances are up and joined cluster, kubelet registered. they have taint node.kubernetes.io/gpu=true:NoSchedule.
micah (runtime): adding toleration to the scheduling policy for in-flight pods so older pending pods can schedule to temp nodes. apply in 2m.
linh (oncall): after toleration patch, starting unsched pods drain -> success. backlog decreasing.
anya (sre): queue dropped from 3200 -> 900 in 8 minutes. token latency back to acceptable ranges.
linh (oncall): any errors during instance boot? jordan?
jordan (infra): initial boots had some IAM warnings but instance profile attached correctly on second try; autoscaler still failing to use new launchtemplate v4 until PassRole is granted.
micah (runtime): customers: we have ~12 customers impacted more than 10% errors. I posted temporary status to status.redwood.ai and bumped priority for the support queue.
linh (oncall): good. putting summary in the bridge: manual nodegroup created w/ LT v3, added 20 GPUs, patched tolerations, queue drained, autoscaler still failing on LT v4 because of missing iam:PassRole.
anya (sre): next action: infra to restore iam:PassRole to autoscaler role for LT v4 or roll back LT reference in ASG. which is lower risk?
jordan (infra): granting PassRole is safe but requires IAM change and code review. rolling the LT reference back on the launch path is lower blast radius and faster. I'll open an emergency change to point the autoscaler to v3 and file the iam change as follow-up.
linh (oncall): sound plan. who owns permanent fix?
anya (sre): infra owns IAM fix. runtime to validate that model routing gracefully degrades when GPU scarce. oncall to coordinate postmortem.
sam (eng): noted — I'll add an autoscaler healthcheck in our deploy pipeline that verifies PassRole coverage for new LT versions.
micah (runtime): customer comms: support message drafted, will escalate to top impacted customers.
linh (oncall): monitoring: keep an eye on GPU reclaim and preemptions — temp ASG is on on-demand for stability. we'll tear it down once autoscaler fixed and normal pools healthy.
anya (sre): check-in in 30m. for now incident status: mitigated -> degraded (customers impacted reduced, service restored to 95% of normal).
linh (oncall): logging final checks: pod failures -> none new, metrics stabilizing. moving to incident timeline and handoff to infra for IAM rollback + CI guard.
jordan (infra): created emergency change CHG-1284 to point autoscaler LT to v3 and created IAM ticket IAM-924 to grant PassRole+conditions. applied autoscaler LT rollback, scaling observed to continue and autoscaler resumed adding nodes.
micah (runtime): all top-10 customers verified OK. support updates sent.
linh (oncall): closing bridge in 10. final notes: root cause — deploy introduced new launch template referencing an instance profile not permitted for autoscaler (PassRole missing). consequence: autoscaler could not create nodes, GPU queue grew and customer requests throttled. mitigation — manual temporary ASG with known-good LT; patched scheduling to drain queue; rolled autoscaler to LT v3; follow-ups assigned.
anya (sre): postmortem owners: infra (jordan) — IAM guard + change control; eng (sam) — deploy pipeline autoscaler checks; runtime (micah) — graceful fallback improvements; oncall (linh) — refine runbook for manual temp nodegroup creation.
linh (oncall): thanks team. I'll file incident ticket and link notes. final check-in: all attendees ack?
jordan (infra): ack.
micah (runtime): ack.
sam (eng): ack.
anya (sre): ack.
linh (oncall): incident closed -> status: mitigated. follow-up meeting scheduled 2026-03-18 15:00 UTC.
